sections.h2: Where is the Jefferson County Recorder, and what does it handle?
sections.html:
The Jefferson County Recorder is at 301 Market Street in Steubenville, OH 43952, and a statewide legal aid directory lists hours of Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The office makes a permanent record of the documents that transfer land, place mortgages and create other charges on it in the county. Ask the office for its current fee schedule before you go.

Jefferson County sits along the Ohio River on the West Virginia line, and Steubenville is both the county seat and its largest city. A deed for any Jefferson County parcel is recorded here, including parcels in Toronto, the county's other city, and in the villages and townships between. Property across the river in Brooke or Hancock County, West Virginia, falls under West Virginia's recording system, not Steubenville's.

sections.h2: How are Jefferson County recording fees built?
sections.html:
R.C. 317.32 sets each recording fee as a base fee plus a matching Ohio housing trust fund fee. Ask the Recorder for the total on your document before you write the check.

  • First two pages of an instrument: a $17 base fee and a $17 housing trust fund fee
  • Each later page of 8.5 by 14 inches or part of one: a $4 base fee and a $4 housing trust fund fee
  • Each marginal reference by a separate instrument: $2 base and $2 housing trust fund
  • A certified copy: $1 base and $1 housing trust fund per page, with a 50 cent plus 50 cent charge for the seal
  • An optional document preservation surcharge of up to $5, kept in the county general fund

The preservation surcharge was added by Senate Bill 94, effective October 24, 2024. Whether Jefferson County applies it, and at what amount up to the cap, is a question for the Recorder.

sections.h2: What conveyance fee applies when a Jefferson County house sells?
sections.html:
Two layers apply, and both are paid to the Auditor before the deed is recorded. The first is the Auditor's own fee under R.C. 319.54(G)(3): one dollar, or ten cents for each hundred dollars or fraction of value, whichever is greater. The second is the county's optional real property transfer tax under R.C. 322.02, capped at thirty cents per hundred dollars.

Jefferson County's 2025 annual financial report refers to a four mill permissive conveyance fee and says the commissioners dedicated one mill of it to the GIS Fund. The Auditor's office is at 301 Market Street, P.O. Box 159, Steubenville, with phone (740) 283-8511 and fax (740) 283-8520. Confirm the rate in force with that office, since commissioners can change a permissive levy by resolution.

The grantor pays, under R.C. 319.202(D). A deed that is a gift or an exempt transfer carries a statement of the reason for the exemption in place of the fee.

sections.h2: Which Jefferson County transfers are exempt from the conveyance fee?
sections.html:
R.C. 319.54(G)(3) lists about two dozen exemptions, and several come up in a family house transfer in Steubenville and the surrounding townships. Each requires the exemption form and sometimes a notarized affidavit.

  • a gift between spouses, or between a parent and child or the spouse of either
  • a transfer among the heirs or devisees of a common decedent when no money is paid
  • a transfer to the trustee of a trust whose grantor kept an unlimited power to revoke it
  • a deed that confirms or corrects a deed already recorded
  • a transfer where the value does not exceed one hundred dollars
  • a transfer under a court order, except where it results from a sale carried out under the order

A sale to an investor is not on the list. Even a quick as-is sale to a cash buyer is a fee-paying transfer, and the fee comes out of the seller's proceeds at closing.

The same report gives the county's 2025 unemployment rate as 4.90% and its population as 63,597, which ranks 39th among Ohio's 88 counties. The county was once a steel center: a rolling mill opened in 1856 and a coal shaft was sunk the same year, per Wikipedia.

sections.h2: What do the numbers say about Jefferson County homes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows 30,964 housing units for July 2025, a 70.5% owner-occupied rate and a median owner-occupied value of $127,800 for 2020 to 2024. Median gross rent is $835, and median household income is $59,055. Persons 65 and over make up 23.9% of the county, the highest share of the four Ohio counties on that comparison, and 17.7% of people live in poverty.

Population fell 2.5% from the April 2020 base to July 2025, the largest decline among those four counties. The Weirton-Steubenville metropolitan area, which includes Brooke and Hancock counties in West Virginia, is the labor market most residents work in.

sections.h2: How does the Auditor step fit with recording in Jefferson County?
sections.html:
The Auditor goes first. R.C. 322.02 says any county transfer tax is paid by the grantor to the county auditor when the deed is delivered and before it is presented to the recorder. The Auditor endorses the deed with the fee amount, and the endorsed deed then moves to the Recorder.

R.C. 317.13 required every Ohio recorder, auditor and engineer to offer an electronic method for recording conveyance papers by June 30, 2026, and that date has passed. A title company in Steubenville can therefore file a closing package electronically instead of walking it across the floor. A seller handling a deed alone should still bring the original, signed and notarized copy if the office asks for paper.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Steubenville and the county?
sections.html:
The United States built Fort Steuben in 1786 to protect surveyors mapping land west of the Ohio River. Settlers built homes around it, and the settlement was first called La Belle and later renamed Steubenville for the fort. Jefferson County was organized on July 29, 1797, six years before Ohio became a state, and assumed its present boundaries in 1833 after neighboring Carroll County was formed.

Ohio Route 7 is the main north-south highway, and Pittsburgh International Airport is reachable east by U.S. Route 22. The county's land area is about 408 square miles, bordered by Columbiana, Belmont, Carroll and Harrison counties and by West Virginia.

faqs.q: Where do I record a deed for a Steubenville house?
faqs.a: At the Jefferson County Recorder, 301 Market Street, Steubenville. Deeds are recorded in the county where the land lies, and Steubenville is in Jefferson County.

faqs.q: Does Jefferson County charge the optional document preservation surcharge?
faqs.a: Ask the Recorder. R.C. 317.32 allows a surcharge of up to five dollars, and the office can tell you what it adds to a deed.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee on a Jefferson County sale?
faqs.a: The seller. R.C. 319.202(D) makes the grantor pay the Auditor's fee under R.C. 319.54(G)(3) and any transfer tax the county has levied under Chapter 322.

faqs.q: Is a gift from a parent to a child exempt from the conveyance fee in Jefferson County?
faqs.a: Yes, under R.C. 319.54(G)(3)(d), a gift between a parent and child or the spouse of either is exempt. The deed still goes to the Auditor with an exemption statement before it is recorded.

faqs.q: What is the 'four mill' fee in Jefferson County's financial report?
faqs.a: It is the county's permissive conveyance fee. The 2025 report says the commissioners dedicated one mill of the four mill fee to the county's GIS Fund, which keeps the parcel maps current.
